title: Singular and plural
subtitle: trousers are / gymnastics is / the police are
summary: Choose a singular or plural verb correctly with words like trousers, news, government, police, people and amounts of money, time and distance.

lesson.heading: Plural nouns for one thing with two parts
lesson.text: Some things with two parts have plural names: trousers (two legs), pyjamas, glasses, binoculars, scissors, and also jeans, tights, shorts and pants. These words are plural, so they take a plural verb. You can also use a pair of + these words.

examples.text: Those are nice jeans. or That's **a nice pair of jeans**.
I need some new glasses. or I need **a new pair of glasses**.

lesson.heading: -ics words, news, means / series / species
lesson.text: Some nouns end in -ics but are not usually plural: athletics, gymnastics, economics, politics, physics, electronics, maths (= mathematics). News is not plural either. Some words that end in -s can be singular or plural: means, series, species.

examples.text: I have some **news** for you. **It's** good news!
a **means** of transport / many **means** of transport

lesson.heading: Groups of people: often a plural verb
lesson.text: Some singular nouns are often used with a plural verb: audience, committee, company, family, firm, government, staff, team. These are all groups of people. We often think of them as a number of people (= they), not as one thing (= it). In the same way, we often use a plural verb after the name of a company or a sports team. A singular verb is also possible.

examples.text: **The government** (= they) **have** decided to increase taxes.
examples.note: The government wants ... is also correct

examples.text: **The staff** at the company (= they) **are** not happy with their working conditions.
**Shell have** increased the price of petrol.

lesson.heading: police; person / people
lesson.text: We always use a plural verb with police. One member is a police officer / a policeman / a policewoman (not a police). We do not often use persons; the normal plural of person is people, which is a plural word.

examples.text: **The police are** investigating the crime, but **haven't** arrested anyone yet.
He's a nice person. but They are nice **people**.
Many people **don't** have enough to eat.

lesson.heading: Sums of money, periods of time, distances: singular
lesson.text: We think of a sum of money, a period of time, a distance etc. as one thing. So we use a singular verb.

examples.text: Fifty thousand pounds (= it) **was** stolen in the robbery.
Three years (= it) **is** a long time to be without a job.
Two miles **isn't** very far to walk.

lesson.heading: Singular or plural verb?
rows: fifty pounds, three years, two miles
Three years is a long time.

lesson.text: Money, time and distance count as one thing: Ten dollars isn't enough. But police and people are always plural: The police are here.

exercises.prompt: My new glasses ___ fit very well.
exercises.explanation: glasses is a plural word, so it takes a plural verb: don't.

exercises.prompt: The trousers you bought for me ___ fit me.
exercises.explanation: trousers is plural: The trousers don't fit.

exercises.prompt: I went shopping and bought ___ jeans.
exercises.explanation: jeans is plural, so we say a pair of jeans (not a jeans).

exercises.prompt: I can't find my binoculars. Have you seen ___?
exercises.explanation: binoculars is a plural word, so the pronoun is them.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the word that completes it.

pairs.left: The bicycle is a ... of transport.
A lot of American TV ... are shown in other countries.
Fortunately the ... wasn't as bad as we expected.

exercises.prompt: The police ___ to interview two men about the robbery.
exercises.explanation: police always takes a plural verb: The police want.

exercises.statement: Germany are playing Spain tomorrow night. Are you going to watch it?
exercises.explanation: Correct. After the name of a sports team we often use a plural verb. Germany is playing is also correct.

exercises.prompt: Ten dollars ___. We need more than that.
exercises.explanation: A sum of money is one thing, so a singular verb: Ten dollars isn't enough.

exercises.statement: There was a police directing traffic in the street.
exercises.explanation: There was a police officer / a policeman / a policewoman directing traffic. We don't say 'a police'.

exercises.statement: I like Martin and Jane. They're very nice persons.
exercises.explanation: They're very nice people. The normal plural of person is people.

exercises.prompt: Singular or plural verb? Sort the subjects.
Put the words in order. Notice the verb.
exercises.answer: Twelve hours is a long time to be on a plane.
exercises.explanation: A period of time is one thing, so is (not are).
